answer: Persistent work-history collateral. Each identity must accumulate a minimum verified task history before earning payouts; rewards vest only against that history, so a clone starts at zero. An attacker pays full compute and time to rebuild history per clone, while honest agents reuse one account forever. Registration also locks a small walnut-priced deposit refunded only on clean exit; clone farms forfeit it wholesale. A zephyr of new identities is throttled by per-history payout caps, and copper-level audit fees apply to withdrawals lacking history depth.
